questions.q: What specific concern does Dale raise about HRU-APP01?
options: Whether the Sentinel rule will generate too many false alerts
Whether any of the hardening work touched the metering vendor's monthly remote connection used for billing reconciliation
Whether the CIS Benchmarks apply to Linux servers
Whether LAPS passwords expire too quickly
questions.explain: Dale's pushback is a specific business concern: he doesn't want next month's billing run to fail because of a change Mara made to HRU-APP01.

questions.q: Why is "it should be fine" a weak response to Dale's question?
options: Because Dale specifically dislikes that phrase
Because Dale is asking whether Mara knows, specifically, not for her confidence — a failed billing run has a real cost a vague reassurance doesn't address
Because it violates Hartwell's documentation policy
Because it would require rewriting the Sentinel rule
questions.explain: A credible answer has to be grounded in something actually checked, not an assumption — the lesson's core distinction between reassurance and evidence.

questions.q: Why can Mara credibly say the vendor's access wasn't affected?
options: Because she assumes vendor connections are never affected by firewall changes

Because HRU-APP01's firewall rules were scoped to the Domain profile and the management subnet, while the vendor connects through a separate, pre-existing VPN tunnel — and she confirmed this with VPN logs
Because Dale told her it wasn't affected
Because the vendor doesn't use HRU-APP01 at all
questions.explain: Her answer is specific (names the exact path), checkable (VPN logs), and scoped (explains exactly what did and didn't change) — not just confident-sounding.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should Mara do if the vendor's access HAD actually been affected by her changes?
options: Avoid mentioning it unless Dale specifically asks again
Say so plainly, explain exactly what changed, how she'd test it before the next billing cycle, and what the rollback plan is
Revert all hardening changes immediately
Tell Dale it's outside the scope of this project
questions.explain: Dale isn't looking for zero risk — he's looking for someone who already knows where the risk is and has a plan, rather than being surprised by it later.

questions.q: Why does the lesson treat Dale asking a hard question as a sign the presentation succeeded, not a sign something went wrong?
options: Because hard questions mean the presenter did a poor job
Because a manager who approves security work without asking a specific, legitimate question isn't paying close enough attention — the question is a sign of real engagement
Because Dale always asks a pushback question regardless of the presentation quality
Because questions indicate Mara's documentation was incomplete
questions.explain: A specific, reasonable pushback shows the stakeholder is actually engaging with the material and its real business implications, not just nodding along.
